messages:
Maya (PM): Quick sync: ordering playbook for the Optimize toolkit features — quantization, batching, caching. Customer asks are piling up and we need a sequencing decision: prioritize by pure impact, by engineering dependency, or follow RICE? Any gut takes or data we should run first?
AJ (Eng): leaning quantization-first. Biggest immediate win for hosted: measured ~30-40% token-cost drop for 8-bit/4-bit on our top models. Effort is mainly conversion tooling + QA. Low infra surface change initially. :money_with_wings:
Chris (Infra): batching is higher infra risk but gives solid p99 latency and throughput improvements for high-concurrency routes. Continuous batching affects runtime and kernel selection — needs careful rollout.
Li (Research): caching gives big wins for prefix-heavy workloads (search, assistant templates). We saw ~25-35% token reduction on two customers in the sample set. Much smaller for highly variable multi-turn chats though.
Evan (Data): did a quick RICE sketch (very rough) this morning: 
- Quantization: Reach=8, Impact=7, Confidence=0.6, Effort=3 -> Score ~= 11.2
- Batching: Reach=9, Impact=6, Confidence=0.5, Effort=4 -> Score ~= 6.75
- Caching: Reach=6, Impact=7, Confidence=0.5, Effort=2 -> Score ~= 10.5
Numbers are rough but point toward quant + caching ahead of batching if we care about cost per token quickly.
Chris (Infra): that aligns with risk profile, but quant can cause quality regressions — we need automated evals + rollback. Also Dedicated customers may require batching optimizations to meet throughput SLOs.
Maya (PM): proposed launch criteria to make decisions objective: either >=15% p50 latency improvement OR >=20% cost-per-token reduction under baseline traffic, AND <=2% quality regression on our core eval prompt set. Canary plan: 1% traffic for 48h, monitor cost_per_token_by_model, p50/p95 latency, and eval regression metrics. If stable, ramp to 10% for 24h then full ramp.
AJ (Eng): ops checklist for a quant MVP: model conversion tooling, model store artifact, feature flag + canary, QA prompt deck, rollback path. Rough estimate: 2-3 sprints for a minimal, safe spike.
Li (Research): I'll assemble eval decks for quant and caching within 1 week — will include targeted adversarial cases to detect subtle regressions.
Evan (Data): I'll add instrumentation and dashboards: cost_per_token_by_model, p50_latency_by_route, eval_regression_pct, and set alerts at 1.5% regression during canary.
Maya (PM): decision flow suggestion: run 2-week timeboxed spikes in parallel (quant spike, caching spike, batching feasibility spike). After spikes we'll reconvene with updated RICE numbers, telemetry, and decide sequence. If quant spike meets confidence + launch criteria, ship quant MVP first, then caching, then batching depending on Dedicated/customer throughput asks.
Chris (Infra): +1
AJ (Eng): +1
Li (Research): +1
Evan (Data): +1
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: run-spike-env for quant-spike at 2024-05-25T09:00Z :rocket:
Maya (PM): thanks all — I'll draft a short PRD with owners/timelines and link it here. Ping if you need alignment before spikes start.
